key_insight: The paper introduces a rate-transfer method that turns finite-time Lyapunov bounds for an associated SDE into finite-time convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient algorithms.
engineering_relevance: This gives optimization practitioners a calculus-based way to derive and verify convergence rates for SGD-like methods, including new algorithm variants, without redoing the full stochastic analysis.
method: Build an SDE that corresponds to the stochastic gradient algorithm.
Prove a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE using calculus.
Transfer the resulting finite-time SDE rate bound back to the discrete algorithm.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method recovers established convergence rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and extends to new algorithms through SDE-based calculus arguments.
watch_item: The approach depends on suitable moment and smoothness conditions plus a valid SDE approximation, so rate guarantees may be harder to apply when assumptions are violated.
paper_title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
